newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Southeast Asia currency falls to help tourism.
newsitem.headline: Southeast Asia currency falls to help tourism.

text.p: Significant falls in the value of Southeast Asian currencies against the dollar in recent weeks will help the region's tourism industry, experts said on Friday.
"We hope devaluation of the (Thai) baht and others is an opportunity to see more overseas tourists," Paisan Wangsai of the Tourism Authority of Thailand told a news conference.

Manila hoped to increase foreign exchange earnings from tourism in 1997 to at least US$3 billion compared to the $US2.7 billion it achieved last year, said Daniel Corpuz of the Philippine Convention and Visitor Corporation.

"We anticipate that the contribution of the U.S. and the attractiveness of the Philippines will be enhanced by the lower exchange rates," Corpuz added. Americans were the backbone of the Philippine industry, he said.
Adrian Lee of the Malaysian Tourism Promotion Board said he also hoped to see more tourists from outside the region whose currencies will now go further in Southeast Asia.
